extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, physicists, and advanced students studying classical geometry and the geometric construction of trajectories (Newtonian-era methods)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric lemmas and constructive procedures for transforming figures, constructing curves (conic sections and given-shaped trajectories) tangent to given lines and passing through given points, and locating bodies on parabolic/elliptic orbits at assigned times. Includes proofs, corollaries, and algorithmic geometric approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of tangency under coordinate scaling/translation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a point G is tangent to a straight line or conic in one figure, the correspondingly transformed point g (under the described proportional coordinate change) is tangent to the correspondingly transformed straight line or conic; the order (analytic degree) of the curves touched is preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace original abscissa and ordinate AD, DG by OA×AB÷ad and OA×dg÷ad respectively in the equation; indeterminates rise to the same number of dimensions so the transformed curve has the same analytic order. Use this to transfer tangency relations between the original and transformed figures. (Includes algebraic justification showing equal analytic order and preservation of tangency.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation preserves tangents and contact points (lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line is tangent to a curved line in the first figure, the translated straight line will be tangent to the corresponding curved line in the translated figure (and conversely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two points of a curve coincide in the original, their translated counterparts coincide in the new figure; hence the lines joining them become tangents in both figures. This is used to transfer tangency information between figures when performing the lemma's transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing problems by transforming figures to simpler ones
rubrics_metrics.description: To transform a rectilinear figure into another, transfer the intersections of straight lines and draw corresponding straight lines in the new figure; to transform a curvilinear figure, transfer points of the curve, tangents and other defining straight lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose for the first ordinate (radius) any straight line which passes through the intersection of converging lines to transform convergents into parallels (viewing intersection tending to infinity). Solve the problem in the transformed (simpler) figure, then apply the inverse operations to recover the solution in the original figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXV (Prob. XVII): Construct trajectory through two given points tangent to three given straight lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a conic (trajectory) that passes through two given points and is tangent to three given lines in given positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the lemma to choose an infinite point (make two of the tangents parallel) so the figure transforms to one where two given tangents are parallel and the third tangent is parallel to the line through the two given points. In the transformed figure find contact points c,d,e using proportions derived from conic-section relations (squares and rectangles). Transfer these contact points back to the original figure by inverse transformation and apply the construction of Problem XIV (case 1) to describe the trajectory. Note: depending on relative positions of points a,b with respect to h,l, choices of contact points inside/outside vary and some configurations make the problem impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXVI (Prob. XVIII): Construct trajectory through a given point tangent to four given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a conic that passes through a given point and is tangent to four given straight lines in given positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intersect common intersections of pairs of tangents to get a straight line to use as first ordinate; transform so that two of the tangents become parallel; in the transformed figure two tangents that previously concur become parallel and then (using earlier propositions) one finds two points through which the conic passes. Apply inverse of Lemma XXII to return points to original figure; then use Prop. XVII to construct the trajectory. (Q.E.F.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXIII: Locating a point cut in a given ratio on a connector of two given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two lines AC, BD terminating at given points A,B and having a given ratio, and the line CD joining indeterminate points C,D is cut in a given ratio at K: point K can be located on a line of given position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find intersection E of AC and BD. On BE take BG such that BG:AE = BD:AC, set FD = EG, produce the similar triangles and cut CF in the given ratio to get L; by completing a parallelogram ELKH one locates K on the side HK which is a line of given position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXIV: Mean-proportional semidiameter for two parallel tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: If three lines are tangent to any conic, of which two are parallel and given in position, then the semidiameter of the conic parallel to those two is the mean proportional between the segments of those tangents intercepted between the contact points and the third tangent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct conjugate diameters and parallelogram IKCL; use similarity of triangles and conic-section proportionalities to derive AF : CD : : CD : BG (i.e., AF, CD, BG in continued proportion). Corollaries give additional proportional relations between segments and distances to center (e.g., AF: BQ :: AP: BG, and FO:OG relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXV: Proportional relations for parallelogram sides tangent to a conic
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram's four infinitely produced sides are tangent to any conic and are cut by any fifth tangent, and abscissas taken at opposite angles are summed, then the abscissa of one side to that side is as the adjacent portion of the adjacent side to that side's abscissa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let a parallelogram MIKL have its sides tangent at A,B,C,D; the fifth tangent intersects sides in F,Q,H,E. Then ME:MI = BK:KQ and KH:KL = AM:MF, etc. Use Corollary results to equate rectangles and find centers. (Includes corollaries about equal rectangles and center-location by bisectors.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXVII (Prob. XIX): Construct trajectory tangent to five given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a trajectory (conic) that is tangent to five given lines in given positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For quadrilaterals formed by four tangents, diagonals bisect, and the line through bisection points passes through the center. Thus find the center O as intersection of bisectors of diagonals from two different quadrilaterals of tangents; draw a line KL parallel to a chosen tangent at such distance that O is midway between parallels; KL will be tangent to the sought trajectory. Intersect KL with other tangents to find contact points and complete construction. (Notes: same method adapts to cases with given centers or asymptotes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXVI: Positioning a specific triangle so its angles touch three given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a triangle of specified shape and size, place it so that its three angles are tangent to three given lines (not all parallel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the triangle's sides describe three circular segments equal to the given angles; extend them to full circles, find intersections and centers P,Q; using similarity and chosen proportional segments (Ga:AB :: GP:PQ) construct points a,b,c. Assemble a figure similar and equal to triangle abcDEF so that its angles touch the prescribed lines. (Gives an explicit circle-segment based construction.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXVIII (Prob. XX): Describe a trajectory of given shape and magnitude whose parts are cut by three given lines in given parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a curve similar and equal to a given curve DEF such that its parts DE and EF are cut by three given lines AB, AC, BC into given parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take the triangle DE F and place it so its angles are tangent to the three given lines using Lemma XXVI; then about that triangle describe a trajectory similar and equal to the given curve. (Q.E.F.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXVII: Construct trapezium of given shape with angles tangent to four given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given four position lines (not all parallel nor concurrent), construct a trapezium of specified shape so that its vertices/angles lie tangent to the four lines respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use circular segment constructions on sides FG, FH, FI so that segments capture prescribed angles; complete circles and take centers P,Q; produce PQ and choose QR on PQ in ratio QR:PQ = BC:AB, then describe a fourth circle to intersect the third; taking intersections a,b,c and joining appropriate lines produces a figure ABCfghi similar to FGHI with desired tangency. The proof uses similarity of polygon PQRK with abcK, comparing ratios and inscribed angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIX (Prob. XIX): Construct trajectory of given shape cut by four lines in specified order/species/proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a trajectory similar to a given curve FGHI whose parts FG, GH, HI are to be intersected by four given position lines AB & AD, AD & BD, BD & EC in the given order and proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First construct a trapezium fghi similar to FGHI whose angles tangent prescribed lines via Lemma XXVII, then about that trapezium describe the trajectory similar to FGHI (Q.E.F.). Scholium presents an alternate construction using auxiliary angles and proportional lines to effect the same result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXX (Prob. XXII): Locate a body on a given parabolic trajectory at an assigned time
rubrics_metrics.description: For motion of a body along a given parabola under a central force, construct the point P on the parabola corresponding to a given elapsed time from the vertex, using area-time proportionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given S (umbilicus) and A (vertex) of the parabola and parameter M, bisect AS at G and erect perpendicular GH of length 3M. With center H and radius HS draw a circle cutting the parabola at the required point P. The proof shows area APS equals 4AS×M and uses algebraic area relations. Corollaries relate GH:AS to time ratios and to velocity relations (e.g., velocity at H : velocity at A = 3:8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXVIII: Impossibility of finite algebraic area-formula for a general oval (irrationality of many curves)
rubrics_metrics.description: No oval exists whose area (with abscissas taken by arbitrary straight lines) can in general be expressed by an equation with a finite number of terms and dimensions; similarly many curve lengths and perimeters cannot be expressed by finite algebraic equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: rotating a chord about a pole generates a spiral with infinitely many intersections with a given line; finite polynomial equations can only give a finite number of intersection roots for given degree, so intersections of such spirals (and hence areas/perimeters of general ovals) cannot be captured by finite algebraic equations. Corollary: area of ellipse as a time-function is not given by a finite equation; distinguishes geometric rational curves (lengths given by algebraic ratios) from geometric irrational curves (e.g., spirals, quadratrices, trochoids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXXI (Prob. XXIII): Locate a body on a given elliptic trajectory at an assigned time (geometric/algorithmic method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an ellipse APB with vertex A and center O (umbilicus S), construct point P corresponding to a given elapsed time using geometric constructions involving trochoids, circles, and iterative angular corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend OA to G with OG:OA = OA:OS, erect GH and roll the circle GEF about GH to describe a trochoid ALI; choose GK in ratio to the trochoid perimeter equal to the time to traverse arc AP relative to one revolution in the ellipse; erect KL perpendicular to intersect trochoid at L and draw LP parallel to KG to meet the ellipse at P. For practical computations use the semicircle construction and successive corrections (angles E, G, I...) to converge to the eccentric anomaly (series ACQ + E + G + I + ...), with rapid convergence (usually only first correction needed). The Scholium gives alternative approximate constructions (semicircle GFO and circle intersections) and Newtonian-style iterative series for astronomical application; also handles limiting hyperbolic/parabolic cases and gives a convergent infinite series procedure for angle correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical computational notes (Scholia) for elliptic/hyperbolic cases
rubrics_metrics.description: For astronomical uses, give specific formulas and practical constructions: use semiaxes AO, OB, OD and side length L to compute auxiliary angles Y,Z and then compute mean motion angle T proportional to time; apply corrections V,X to get the 'equal' (mean-motion-equal) angle BHP and then find point P where abscissa SP cuts off area BSP approximately proportional to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains approximations: choose small-angle approximations for V and X when they are tiny (seconds), advises how to alternate signs on corrections if intermediate quantities are negative, and suggests iterative refinement and alternatives (hyperbola) via analogous constructions. Recommends practical truncation because series converges quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section heading guidance: Use previous lemmas to find axes, umbilics, centers after trajectory is constructed
rubrics_metrics.description: After describing a trajectory, axes and umbilici (centers of curvature etc.) may be located by constructions involving moving angles, poles and normals: rotate the pair of movable legs keeping them parallel to retrace the generating circle and find centers/intersections to locate major/minor axes and umbilici.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct circles through concurrency points of rotating legs, draw normals from circle center to the regulating line MN, drop perpendiculars to locate K (regula's proper point); where rotated legs concur at K, the first pair's legs are parallel to major axis and perpendicular to minor; reversing yields axes and umbilics directly. Also notes trapezoid-inscription consequences and other lemmas for further constructions.
